subject: pharmacology
title: Inhaled Anaesthetics: Halothane, Isoflurane, Sevoflurane, Desflurane, Nitrous Oxide and MAC

steps.tx: Volatile anaesthetics are dosed in **MAC** (minimum alveolar concentration), the alveolar concentration at one atmosphere preventing movement in half of patients after surgical incision, the anaesthetic ED50 that lets potencies be compared on one scale. MAC falls with age, hypothermia, opioids, pregnancy and acute alcohol intoxication, and rises in infants, hyperthermia and chronic alcohol use. Additivity means half a MAC of each of two agents approximates one MAC together.
steps.say: MAC is the common currency of inhaled potency; age, temperature and opioids move the exchange rate.

left.title: MAC landmarks (young adult)
points: Desflurane about 6 percent, sevoflurane about 2 percent
Isoflurane about 1.2 percent, halothane about 0.75 percent
Nitrous oxide about 104 percent: impossible alone at sea level
MAC awake roughly a third of MAC for incision

right.title: MAC modifiers
points: Lower: age, hypothermia, opioids, pregnancy, acute alcohol
Higher: infancy, hyperthermia, chronic alcohol, hypernatraemia
Additive between inhaled agents and nitrous oxide
MAC BAR (blocking autonomic response) exceeds MAC

steps.tx: **Halothane**, the potent prototype (MAC 0.75), smooth and non pungent enough for inhalational induction in children historically, sensitises the myocardium to catecholamines so adrenaline infiltrations provoke ventricular arrhythmias, depresses contractility and respiration dose dependently, and relaxes uterus usefully and hazardously by turns. Its metabolism of about 20 percent, highest of the volatiles, underlies its immune hepatitis in the next lessons. Modern practice retired it where successors are stocked.
steps.say: Halothane is potent and pleasant and sensitises the heart to adrenaline; that trilogy retired it.

vis.caption: Sites of action of inhaled and intravenous general anaesthetics, the shared stage for this module's agents.

steps.tx: **Isoflurane** (MAC 1.2) trades halothane's smoothness for pungency that forbids inhalational induction, then repays with minimal metabolism (0.2 percent), cardiovascular stability and coronary vasodilatation gentle enough for cardiac surgery tradition. **Sevoflurane** (MAC 2) is non pungent and sweet smelling, the modern inhalational induction agent for children, with low blood solubility for fast in and out; its soda lime degradation product compound A frightened rats more than patients, with fresh gas flow guidance as the residue.
steps.say: Isoflurane is stable and pungent, sevoflurane is sweet and swift; induction belongs to sevoflurane now.

left.title: Isoflurane
points: MAC about 1.2 percent, pungent, no mask induction
Minimal metabolism, organ friendly
Vasodilatation with preserved cardiac output
Workhorse maintenance agent for decades

right.title: Sevoflurane
points: MAC about 2 percent, non pungent and well tolerated
Agent of choice for paediatric inhalational induction
Low blood gas solubility: rapid induction and emergence
Compound A with soda lime: use adequate fresh gas flows

steps.tx: **Desflurane** (MAC 6) is the least potent and least blood soluble volatile, giving the fastest emergence and minute to minute control prized in long cases and obesity, at the price of pungency, airway irritation with coughing and laryngospasm on induction, sympathetic surges when concentrations jump quickly, and a heated vaporiser because it boils near room temperature. Its greenhouse potency also makes it the environmental villain of the family in modern theatre audits.
steps.say: Desflurane wakes fastest and irritates most; titrate it gently and expect the vaporiser to be warm.

nodes.label: Lowest blood solubility of the volatiles
Alveolar and brain tensions track the dial within minutes
Fastest emergence and recovery room turnover

steps.tx: **Desflurane** has a MAC of 6, so it is the least potent volatile, and it is also the least soluble in blood, which gives the fastest waking and the tightest minute to minute control in long operations and in obesity. It is pungent, so induction provokes coughing and laryngospasm, and a rapid jump in concentration causes a sympathetic surge. The vaporiser is heated because the liquid boils near room temperature. In theatre environmental audits its greenhouse effect is the worst of the family.
steps.say: Desflurane is weak and poorly soluble, so waking is fastest and the level can be changed minute by minute, which helps in long cases and obesity. Airway irritation makes induction cough or spasm, and a sudden increase drives a sympathetic surge. The vaporiser must be heated because the drug boils at room temperature, and its climate impact is the highest among volatiles.

vis.alt: A heated desflurane vaporiser is mounted on an anaesthetic machine beside a curve of very rapid emergence.
vis.caption: A warmed vaporiser delivers desflurane, and the blood level falls steeply as soon as the vapour is turned off. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Nitrous oxide**, MAC near 104 percent, can never reach surgical anaesthesia alone at atmospheric pressure, yet at 50 to 70 percent it contributes analgesia, anxiolysis (Entonox in labour and procedures) and half a MAC of anaesthetic sparing. It diffuses into air filled spaces faster than nitrogen leaves, expanding bowel, pneumothorax, middle ear and intracranial air, and oxidises vitamin B12's cobalt, inactivating methionine synthase with prolonged or repeated exposure. Diffusion hypoxia on discontinuation closes the next lesson.
steps.say: Nitrous oxide is an analgesic partner, never a solo anaesthetic, and it inflates every air pocket it meets.

left.title: Nitrous oxide contributions
points: Analgesia and anxiolysis at 50 percent (Entonox)
Second gas effect speeding volatile uptake (next lesson)
MAC sparing for co administered volatiles
Minimal cardiovascular and respiratory depression

right.title: Nitrous oxide hazards
points: Expands bowel, pneumothorax, middle ear and air emboli
Inactivates vitamin B12 with prolonged exposure
Diffusion hypoxia when stopped abruptly
Supports combustion and pollutes theatre air

steps.tx: All potent volatiles trigger **malignant hyperthermia** in genetically susceptible ryanodine receptor mutants: uncontrolled sarcoplasmic calcium release, rigidity, hypercapnia out of proportion, hyperthermia late, and death without dantrolene. Succinylcholine shares the trigger list; propofol, opioids, nitrous oxide and non depolarising relaxants are safe. Theatre readiness (dantrolene stocked, vapour free machines) is a systems obligation that examinations test as management, not trivia.
steps.say: Volatiles and succinylcholine trigger malignant hyperthermia; dantrolene and a vapour free machine are the rescue.

nodes.label: Volatile or succinylcholine in susceptible muscle
Ryanodine receptor calcium release runs away
Rigidity, soaring CO2, acidosis, then hyperthermia
Stop trigger, dantrolene, cooling and intensive care

steps.tx: **Cardiovascular signatures** separate the family at the bedside: halothane depresses contractility and sensitises to arrhythmias, isoflurane and sevoflurane vasodilate with reflex heart rate preservation, desflurane adds sympathetic spikes on rapid increases, and all blunt hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction modestly and depress respiration with a characteristic rapid shallow pattern and lost CO2 responsiveness. Coronary steal by isoflurane, long feared in theory, proved clinically negligible at ordinary doses.
steps.say: Halothane weakens and sensitises, the ethers dilate, desflurane surges; all of them quiet the breathing drive.

left.title: Cardiac profiles
points: Halothane: contractility down, catecholamine arrhythmias
Isoflurane and sevoflurane: vasodilatation, output preserved
Desflurane: sympathetic surges with rapid rises
All: dose dependent respiratory depression

right.title: Organ footnotes
points: Uterine relaxation dose dependent across volatiles
Cerebral vasodilatation raises intracranial pressure modestly
Halothane hepatitis and sevoflurane compound A histories
Trigger free technique for malignant hyperthermia families

steps.tx: **Choosing a volatile** is applied pharmacokinetics: sevoflurane to induce children and maintain most lists, desflurane where rapid precise emergence pays (obesity, neurosurgery, long cases), isoflurane as the economical stable veteran, nitrous oxide as analgesic partner where its expansion hazards permit, and halothane remembered for its hepatitis and arrhythmia examinations. The next lesson formalises the solubility physics (blood gas partition coefficients) that predicts each agent's speed.
steps.say: Match the agent to the airway, the abdomen and the clock; the physics lesson next explains why those matches work.

left.title: Speed ranking (fastest first)
points: Desflurane: lowest blood solubility
Sevoflurane: close second, induction friendly
Isoflurane: intermediate
Halothane: slower and most tissue soluble

right.title: Choice anchors
points: Children's mask induction: sevoflurane
Obesity and rapid turnover: desflurane
Cardiac stability tradition: isoflurane
Examination hazards: halothane hepatitis, arrhythmias
